why: The commands are literally push (U) and pop (O) on a last-in-first-out structure; the only work beyond the stack itself is tokenising the string and stopping at X.
hints: Split the string on any whitespace first; the numbers after U are separate tokens, and they may be negative.
Walk the tokens with an index: on U read the next token as the value and push it, on O pop and record, on X stop.
A Python list is the stack (append / pop). One pass over at most 10^4 tokens: O(n) time, O(n) space.
pitfalls: Splitting on a single space breaks on tabs, newlines or repeated spaces; use split() with no argument.
Values left on the stack at X are not output.
The value after U is its own token: advance the index by two, not one.
